claims.text: docker compose up creates and starts the containers for every service in the Compose file on the one Docker engine (daemon) the CLI talks to; Compose's own docs describe deployment on a single host.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: docker compose up; Compose intro features-uses (Single host deployments)

claims.text: The Compose restart key defaults to no. With restart: always, the Docker engine on that same machine starts the container again after it stops, and when the engine itself restarts (e.g. after a reboot, once the engine runs); never on another machine.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Compose file reference services.md restart; docker run --restart (restart policies)

claims.text: docker-compose.yml at stage-1 has no restart: key (grep -c 'restart:' prints 0), so after the host reboots its containers stay stopped until someone runs scripts/up.sh again.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1 docker-compose.yml; Docker docs restart policy default no

claims.text: Compose does not scale a service beyond one container if the Compose file specifies container_name; attempting it is an error.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Compose file reference services.md container_name

claims.text: docker-compose.yml@stage-1: every service has container_name (git show stage-1:docker-compose.yml | grep -n container_name: prints 5 lines: donhang-lab, -web, -db, -api, -app-web); api (lines 81-99) has ipv4_address 172.28.0.13 and no field choosing a machine.
A user-defined bridge network such as donhang exists on one Docker engine only; containers on another host's engine cannot join it.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Networking > bridge network driver (single host)

claims.text: docker compose up starts every container on the one Docker engine it talks to; nothing in Đơn Hàng's docker-compose.yml chooses a machine, and docker compose up cannot spread copies of api over several engines; a second machine needs its own Compose run.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Compose intro (single host); Compose file reference services

claims.text: Kubernetes runs containerized workloads across a group of machines from a declared desired state, restarts failed containers and replaces containers (self-healing).
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Overview (Why you need Kubernetes, Self-healing)

claims.text: When a machine (node) fails, Kubernetes notices it stops reporting and the workload's controller starts replacement containers on other machines.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Architecture > Nodes (node status, heartbeats, eviction); Overview self-healing

claims.text: Kubernetes runs standard container images such as those docker build produces, pulled from a registry by each machine; the Dockerfile does not change.
claims.source_hint: kubernetes.io: Concepts > Containers > Images; Container runtimes

claims.text: caddy:2.10.0 (service web) and postgres:17.6-alpine (service db) are pulled from Docker Hub (no registry host in the name); donhang-api:stage-1 is built locally and would need a push to a reachable registry.
Opinion: when one small system on one machine is enough and brief downtime on reboot is acceptable, Compose can stay; an orchestrator pays off once several machines or copies must be kept running.
claims.source_hint: outline item 5; kubernetes.io Overview (What Kubernetes is not)
